confidence: moderate — directional/magnitude reconstruction, not a closed-form reproduction of the leaf (see limitations)

what_the_leaf_is.quantity: wasted portion of a single heal in a coupled multi-participant (roster) fight: overheal = heal_amount - min(heal_amount, missing_health_at_that_instant)
what_the_leaf_is.identity: heal_amount = effective_heal + overheal; overheal is a *difference* of two simulation-path quantities, so it is highly leveraged in the cumulative damage the healed participant has taken before the event
what_the_leaf_is.index: healing_events[55] is the 56th healing event of the fight, i.e. deep into the coupled timeline

independent_computation.limitation_stated_up_front: The scenario input tuple (roster champions, levels, ranks, items, fight window) for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' lives in scripts/golden_snapshot.py, which is outside the permitted evidence tree; it is not present anywhere under data/ (grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster', 'roster', 'coupled_scenarios' over the whole export returns no scenario definition). A bit-exact recomputation of the 56th healing event of a coupled 5v5 timeline is therefore not possible from the sourced data alone. What IS independently computable from the export is (a) the exact governing constants of the two named items, (b) the exact mathematical identity the engine is documented to owe for Black Cleaver's stack ramp, and (c) the sign and order of magnitude of the resulting change in the healed participant's missing health, which decides which of the two candidate values is consistent.

step_1_item_constants_from_cached_wiki_t.black_cleaver_carve: 6% armor reduction per stack, stacking up to 5 times (30% max), 6 s duration, applied by dealing physical damage to an enemy champion (data/items.json id 3071, passives[0].branches[0])
step_1_item_constants_from_cached_wiki_t.bloodsong_expose_weakness: Spellblade proc; on a champion it inflicts Expose Weakness for 4 s, 'causing them to take 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) increased damage from all sources', 1.5 s cooldown (data/items.json id 3877, passives[0].branches[0])
step_1_item_constants_from_cached_wiki_t.note: Neither item heals. Every healing event in this scenario is a champion/rune/other-item heal whose *waste* is decided by the health path, and both named items are pure damage amplifiers acting on that health path — the scenario is constructed to exercise exactly that coupling.

step_2_exact_identity_owed_for_the_cleav.quoted_source: docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 item 2: 'Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes. ... Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean ... (changing it re-tunes every BC fight in the corpus).'
step_2_exact_identity_owed_for_the_cleav.constant_model: 0.8 * 5 = 4.0 stacks = 24.0% armor reduction, independent of fight length

exact_cesaro_mean_C_eq_5.consequence: for any fight longer than ~10 damaging hits — which a roster fight carrying 56+ healing events certainly is — the exact mean is STRICTLY LARGER than the 0.8*max constant, i.e. more armor shred, more physical damage taken by the shredded participant, LESS missing-health headroom left for the next heal, hence SMALLER overheal. The cap is respected either way (28.5% < 30%).

step_3_mitigation_arithmetic.identity_quoted: docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.1: m(R) = 100/(100+R); reduce_resistance applies flat then percent, percent reduction only while R > 0
step_3_mitigation_arithmetic.worked_example_target_armor_100: 24% reduction -> 76 armor -> m = 100/176 = 0.5682; 27% reduction -> 73 armor -> m = 100/173 = 0.5780; physical-damage uplift = 0.5780/0.5682 - 1 = +1.73%
step_3_mitigation_arithmetic.bloodsong_amp_for_comparison: Expose Weakness is a flat +8% (melee holder) / +5% (ranged holder) multiplier on ALL damage the marked target takes while the 4 s debuff is up

step_4_reconciling_the_observed_leaf_cha.requirement: at fixed heal size, the healed participant must have 54.3 MORE missing health at event 55 than before
step_4_reconciling_the_observed_leaf_cha.sensitivity: with a physical-damage uplift u on the damage that participant has absorbed, the extra missing health is u * D_cumulative. Solving 54.3 = u * D gives D = 3139 at u = 1.73% (armor-100 Cleaver case), D = 2715 at u = 2%, D = 679 at u = 8% (an Expose Weakness amp that was previously not being applied at all).
step_4_reconciling_the_observed_leaf_cha.plausibility: a participant 56 healing events deep into a coupled roster fight has plausibly absorbed on the order of 1000-3500 damage, so BOTH candidate mechanisms (exact Cesaro Cleaver mean replacing the 0.8*max constant in a >10-hit fight, or the Bloodsong Expose Weakness amp being applied where it previously was not) land the observed 54.3 shift squarely in range. Both mechanisms move damage UP and therefore overheal DOWN — the direction of the observed change.
step_4_reconciling_the_observed_leaf_cha.counter_direction_check: For the OLD value to be the correct one, the change would have to have wrongly INCREASED damage on the healed participant — e.g. carrying Carve past its 5-stack / 30% cap, applying the melee 8% Expose Weakness value to a ranged holder, or letting percentage armor reduction drive armor below 0. The wiki text caps Carve at 30% and the exact Cesaro mean tops out at 28.5% (h -> inf gives 5 - 10/h < 5 stacks), so the mathematically exact model cannot breach the cap; and docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 item 3 records that the engine already refuses percentage reduction on non-positive armor per the wiki rule ('Flat armor reduction can reduce armor values below 0, while percentage armor reduction cannot'). No sourced constant in the export supports a damage increase larger than the mechanisms above, so no reading of the cached wiki text vindicates the 97.6 figure.

step_5_secondary_signal.observation: 97.6 is a suspiciously 'whole-heal' shaped number for the 56th heal of a fight: an overheal that equals essentially the entire heal implies the healed participant was still at (or within a hair of) full health that late in a coupled fight, which is what an under-applied damage amplifier looks like. 43.3 is a partial waste, i.e. the participant is genuinely damaged at that instant — the expected shape once the shred/amp is priced.
step_5_secondary_signal.corroborating_magnitudes_from_the_export: data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json shows sourced single-heal magnitudes in this engine of the same order (Aatrox Umbral Dash 276.4 and 50.4, Rengar Battle Roar grey-health 97.2 and 25.4, support heals 155.0 / 165.0 / 350.0), so a heal whose wasted portion is 43.3-97.6 is dimensionally ordinary either way; the magnitude alone does not discriminate, only the direction argument above does.

independent_computation.conclusion: Every mechanism the cached wiki text and the quoted Section 2.3 identity permit for this scenario pushes the healed participant's missing health UP and hence the overheal DOWN, by an amount whose order of magnitude matches the observed 54.3 drop; nothing sourced supports the higher figure. The new value 43.3 is the one consistent with the sourced item constants and the exact Cesaro-mean identity the document itself names as the correct model (the 24% constant it replaces is explicitly labelled APPROX, '+/-20% at the extremes').

sources_quoted.text: Dealing physical damage to an enemy champion applies a stack of Carve for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts 6% armor reduction, up to 30% at 5 stacks.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals 100% base AD bonus physical damage on-hit. If the target is a champion, inflict them with Expose Weakness for 4 seconds, causing them to take 8%/5% increased damage from all sources (1.5 second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sourced healing-event magnitudes used as a dimensional cross-check (Umbral Dash 276.4 / 50.4 at 16% of post-mitigation damage doubled by World Ender; Battle Roar grey health 97.2 / 25.4; support heals 155.0 / 165.0 / 350.0)

limitations: The scenario input tuple for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is defined in scripts/golden_snapshot.py, outside the permitted evidence tree, and appears nowhere under data/ — so this receipt reconstructs the sign and magnitude of the leaf change from sourced constants and the quoted exact identity rather than recomputing 43.3 digit-for-digit.

Because overheal is a difference (heal minus missing health), it is a leveraged downstream quantity: no single wiki formula pins it. The verdict rests on (a) the exact Cesaro-mean identity the foundations document names as correct versus the 0.8*max_stacks constant it labels APPROX, (b) the 5-stack / 30% Carve cap and the 8%/5% Expose Weakness constants, and (c) the arithmetic that a ~1.7-8% damage uplift over 700-3100 absorbed damage yields exactly the observed 54.3 shift.
